summary: The core is built around a module for the Konami 005885 custom chip, with the chip's pins as ports (NXCS, NIOC, VCF/VCB/VCD, OCF/OCB/OCD, COL, NFIR/NIRQ/NNMI). Board parts are instantiated by PCB location (u13A, u11E, u5E...). Video is a per-pixel scan pipeline: H-counter bit edges latch the tile attributes and ROM data, a shift register applies fine scroll, sprites go through a double-buffered line buffer, and a single 5-bit COL mux feeds the color PROMs. None of this follows MAME's draw_sprites/screen_update/tilemap structure. Interrupts and the HUD window come from raster counter bits and positions, not from MAME's scanline callback or its clip-rectangle redraw.

findings.signal: module per custom chip with pin-named ports
findings.mame_ref: finalizr.cpp: finalizr_state (no 005885 device; video split across get_*_tile_info/draw_sprites/screen_update)
findings.note: All of the video, sync, IRQ and clock logic sits in one k005885 module with chip pins as ports (NCK2, NCPE/NCPQ, NIOC, NXCS, VCF/VCB/VCD, OCF/OCB/OCD, COL). MAME has no 005885 abstraction for this game.

findings.signal: board-location instance names and external PROM/ROM topology
findings.where: rtl/Finalizer.sv (KONAMI1 u13A, eprom_* u9C/u12C/u13C/u5E/u5F/u6E..u7F, prom_1 u11F, prom_2 u10F, prom_3 u2F, prom_4 u3F, sn76489 u7C, t8049 u8A)
findings.note: Each ROM, PROM and sound chip is a separate instance named by its board position. The tile and sprite LUT PROMs are wired as external chips addressed by the 005885's VCF/VCB and OCF/OCB pins.

findings.signal: per-pixel tilemap fetch pipeline timed by H-counter bits
findings.note: The VRAM address is formed from counter bits ({tile1_en, h_cnt[2], vpos[7:3], hpos[7:3]}). Attribute, code and ROM data are latched on rising and falling edges of h_cnt[2]/h_cnt[1], and fine scroll is a 32-bit pixel shift register tapped by the low scroll bits. MAME instead builds two whole tilemaps from tile_info callbacks.

findings.signal: HUD as a raster window, not a clipped second draw pass
findings.mame_ref: finalizr.cpp: screen_update (fg_tilemap drawn after sprites into a 40-px clip rect)
findings.note: The second tile layer is chosen by an h_cnt range (tile1_en) with a fixed scroll value, scroll is inhibited and tile priority forced over sprites by further h_cnt windows. MAME instead draws bg, then sprites, then redraws fg in a clip rectangle.

findings.signal: sprite engine as per-line scan into a double-buffered line buffer
findings.note: A state machine reads each 5-byte sprite entry during the line, tests vertical overlap with sprite_vpos, and writes pixels into a line buffer whose bank is chosen by sprite_vpos[0]. It writes only non-zero pixels and clears on read-out. MAME instead loops over all sprites per frame with gfx->transpen and per-size branches.

findings.signal: sprite geometry as gates, not MAME's flip arithmetic
findings.mame_ref: finalizr.cpp: draw_sprites (sx = 256 - sx, sy = 224 - sy, code + 0..3 per quadrant)
findings.note: Sprite size picks which counter bits (ly[3], lx[3], ly[4], lx[4]) replace code bits in the ROM address. Flipscreen is XORed into individual height and width bits. MAME uses per-size offsets such as 280/272/248/240 and up to four separate transpen calls.

findings.signal: behavior MAME leaves unknown: sprite X bit 8 select
findings.mame_ref: finalizr.cpp: draw_sprites ('(sr[offs + 4] & 0x02) is used, meaning unknown'; sx = 41 + sr[3] - (sr[4]&1)<<8)
findings.note: The HDL uses attribute bit 1 to choose between VRAM bit 0 and an AND of X[7:3] for X bit 8. MAME ignores bit 1 and uses a subtraction with a +41 offset.

findings.mame_ref: finalizr.cpp: scanline (scanline == 240 IRQ, scanline % 32 NMI, HOLD_LINE)
findings.note: NMI fires on the falling edge of v_cnt[5] (v_cnt[4] in 280-wide mode), IRQ on the VBLANK edge, and FIRQ on every other VBLANK from a frame toggle flip-flop. Each is a mask-cleared latch, unlike MAME's scanline-number test with no FIRQ.
h_cnt reloads to 128 after 511 and v_cnt runs from about 248 to 510, with blanking and sync decoded at fixed counter values. MAME uses a 0-based visible area.

findings.signal: color mixer produces PROM address with layer bit
findings.note: A single mux picks tile or sprite by sprite transparency or the tile-priority window, and outputs COL = {sel, 4-bit pixel} straight into the color PROMs. MAME gets the same result through indirect pen tables.

findings.signal: bootleg MCU T1 driven from divided T0 clock
findings.where: rtl/Finalizer.sv (snd01_timer counter on t0_o feeding t1_i)
findings.note: A counter on the MCU's T0 output drives T1, wired the way the board would be. MAME approximates this with an emulated-time read.

findings.signal: memory map, register addresses and I/O decode
findings.note: The register offsets 0-4, the 0x0800-0x081d I/O map and the sound IRQ set/clear (0x81c write, port2 bit 7 clear) match MAME, as any correct core must. Decode uses the chip's NIOC output.

findings.signal: FPGA engineering (sprite cache, split ROM ports, bootleg options)
findings.note: A sprite RAM cache gives the one-frame sprite delay, and dual-ported ROMs serve tiles and sprites at once. Both are resource and timing engineering, and are not counted either way.
